question: Pruning is a means of model compression that can improve model efficiency in NLP. What are some recent general, task-agnostic pruning methods for large language methods that have worked well?

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer situates pruning as a model compression technique for billion-scale LLMs, dropping a subset of weights or sub-networks to improve efficiency while preserving performance.
examples: LLMs with billions of parameters are natural candidates for network pruning
Pruning drops weights while striving to preserve performance

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer frames the discussed methods as task-agnostic (pruned on pretraining data or general-purpose, without task-specific specialization) and describes at least two distinct recent methods (e.g., Sheared-LLaMA and Wanda) rather than a single one.
examples: Task-agnostic pruning prunes a model on pretraining data
Sheared-LLaMA and Wanda are two recent effective task-agnostic pruning approaches

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer distinguishes structured pruning (removing layers, heads, intermediate/hidden dimensions) from unstructured or semi-structured pruning when positioning the methods.
examples: Structured pruning removes larger blocks like layers or attention heads
Sheared-LLaMA performs structured pruning; Wanda induces sparsity without retraining

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer presents Sheared-LLaMA as a recent structured pruning approach that creates smaller LLMs from larger pretrained models via two key techniques: targeted structured pruning (removing layers, heads, and intermediate/hidden dimensions end-to-end to a target shape) and dynamic batch loading (adjusting batch composition based on varying domain losses) during continual pretraining.
examples: Sheared-LLaMA prunes LLaMA2-7B down to 1.3B and 2.7B parameter models
Targeted structured pruning removes layers, heads, and intermediate and hidden dimensions to a specified target shape
Dynamic batch loading updates batch composition based on varying losses across domains

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites evidence that Sheared-LLaMA models outperform same-size open-source models (e.g., Pythia, INCITE, OpenLLaMA, TinyLlama) at only ~3% of the compute cost of training from scratch.
examples: Sheared-LLaMA beats equivalent-size models at only 3% of pretraining compute
It outperforms models like Pythia and TinyLlama on downstream and instruction-tuning evaluations

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies Wanda as a simple, effective pruning method that induces sparsity in pretrained LLMs with no retraining or weight updates; the pruned LLM can be used as is.
examples: Wanda (Pruning by Weights and activations) prunes pretrained LLMs directly
No retraining or weight update is needed; the pruned model is used immediately after pruning

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains Wanda's mechanism: pruning weights with the smallest product of weight magnitude and corresponding input activation, on a per-output basis, motivated by emergent large-magnitude features in LLMs.
examples: Wanda prunes weights with the smallest magnitude times input activation on a per-output basis
The approach is motivated by the observation of emergent large magnitude features in LLMs

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that Wanda significantly outperforms magnitude pruning and is competitive with methods requiring intensive weight updates, evaluated on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 benchmarks.
examples: Wanda significantly outperforms the magnitude pruning baseline on LLaMA benchmarks
It performs competitively against recent methods involving intensive weight updates

ingredients.name: valuable_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer conveys the overall takeaway that pruning existing LLMs (versus training smaller models from scratch) is a cost-effective path to efficient, high-performing models.
examples: Structured pruning of existing LLMs is far more cost-effective than training from scratch
Both methods demonstrate that compression of pretrained LLMs can match or beat same-size trained models
